record.file_problem: Repository metadata and README are present; code and notebook were not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports a refusal outcome after a weight-space projection edit based on harmful-versus-harmless activation differences. This tests refusal removal with a different intervention from the original activation ablation and addition.
record.gate_note: The README says many built-in example prompts show compliance after abliteration where the baseline showed refusal or heavy disclaimers. It gives no counts or scores. The README also describes the edit as per-layer and notes that the method does not test adding a direction or preservation of general abilities. It references demo captures, but their contents are not available in the supplied text.
record.test_reason: The README applies a norm-preserving, per-layer abliteration weight edit to the released Gemma 4 E2B IT model. It reports, qualitatively, that many refusal-triggering example prompts get compliance after the edit. This is a new-model check of V2. It reports no counts or rates, and the method is a per-layer variant rather than V1's single direction.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct as paraphrased. The README presents per-layer, norm-preserving weight projection as a way to reduce Gemma 4 E2B IT refusals. It cautions that refusal is high-rank and contextual, that the difference of means may carry dataset confounds, and that its eval is a coarse substring check.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a weight-space edit to o_proj and down_proj with separate per-layer directions, winsorization, orthogonalization, and row-norm restoration; the README identifies the approach with upstream norm-preserving biprojected abliteration, not the original activation ablation-and-addition procedure. Repository type: tool/study implementation.
record.problems: Only qualitative refusal/compliance is reported in the README, without counts, rates, uncertainty, or general-capability evaluation. The README describes substring heuristics as coarse and notes possible dataset confounds and high-rank, contextual refusal behavior.
record.rows_left_out: No additional result rows in the supplied README text. The referenced demo captures and code are not available for inspection here.

untested.parts: Not tested: single shared direction, activation ablation, inducing refusal by adding the direction, and preservation of other abilities.
Not tested: a quantified refusal rate before and after the edit, general capability or coherence after the edit, and released models other than Gemma 4 E2B IT.
The README asserts refusal is 'high-rank and contextual' but reports no result on it.

missing.what: Substring-heuristic refusal evaluation results from the eval scripts (scripts/evaluate.py, deploy/evaluate.py); the README reports no numbers from them
Before/after demo captures EX1 and EX2 (image contents not available as text)

record.verdict_notes: This is a hobby or tool repository with no quantitative results. It follows TrevorS/gemma-4-abliteration and is not peer reviewed. The verdict rests only on one qualitative README sentence. Relation could arguably be T4, since it largely reports its own tool working. It is kept as a weak V2 test because V2 is precisely abliteration's effect on a released model.

versions.untested_parts: Tests only removal via a weight edit using separate per-layer directions. Does not test activation ablation at every position, adding a direction, or whether other abilities remain intact.
Reports a qualitative result for one model and built-in example prompts only; does not quantify refusal removal or test other released models.
Does not test jailbreak suppression of the direction or training against its ablation.
The README calls refusal high-rank and contextual, but reports no result testing affine, cone, or multiple-direction representations.
Does not test whether harmfulness judgment and refusal are separately encoded.
Does not test transfer across languages, model variants, or base and instruct models.

rows.subject: Gemma 4 E2B IT
rows.operation_detail: Project per-layer refusal-related directions out of o_proj and down_proj, then restore row norms.

conditions.value: Built-in example prompts, described as the same family as scripts/config.py

rows.baseline: Baseline showed refusal or heavy disclaimers.
rows.value: After abliteration, many prompts show compliance.
rows.note: The README reports this outcome qualitatively and does not state a prompt count or rate. The tested edit uses separate directions per layer; it is not the original single activation-direction ablation/addition.
rows.check: Should link to V2 only. The edit uses a separate, orthogonalized difference-of-means direction for each of the 35 layers, not V1's single direction. It involves no activation ablation, no direction addition and no capability check, so it cannot bear on V1. The state is 'partial' only because the README says 'many' prompts comply, implying not all. No count or rate is given, so the evidence is anecdotal.
